brief.headline: Push for ₹7.62/NOS on the 250 mL amber PET bottle to close an 11.5% gap — we're already paying that to TPAC

priceAsk.summary: Match the best price we already pay: ₹7.62/NOS for the PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01
priceAsk.target: ₹7.62/NOS (saves ₹7.19 L/year on that SKU alone; total upside ₹8.48 L/year across the basket)
priceAsk.basis: We pay TPAC Packaging India Pvt Ltd. ₹7.62/NOS for the identical bottle. PIK charges us ₹8.49/NOS — an 11.5% premium for the same item. Market research shows 28 mm induction-wad PP cap pricing is MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume, so the ₹7.62 benchmark is well within range.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 days after receipt — no change needed

brief.financialLeverage: PIK Plastics publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is meaningful to a private converter, but without their numbers we can't gauge exactly how much. The leverage comes from our data: we have a proven lower price in-house (₹7.62 from TPAC) and four strong alternate suppliers ready to quote — Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) and Mold-Tek Packaging (₹1010.97 Cr, score 73/100) are both bigger, healthier firms who can step in. That competition is our main lever, not their balance sheet.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹8.48 L/year versus the best prices we already have
PIK's price for the 250 mL amber PET bottle is 11.5% above TPAC's
TPAC supplies the same bottle at ₹7.62/NOS; PIK charges ₹8.49/NOS
Closing the gap on that one SKU alone saves us ₹7.19 L/year
Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate already on our radar.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health score 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging. Strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand, ₹19.83 Cr revenue) — direct fit for our PET bottles, though smaller and health score is lower at 24/100.

risks: PIK's financials are private, so we can't see early warnings of cash trouble or capacity constraints — monitor delivery and quality closely if we push hard on price.
If PIK won't move to ₹7.62, we risk needing to shift ₹1.92 Cr of volume mid-year — line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek quotes now so the alternate is real, not a bluff.
The 11.5% gap is large and obvious; if PIK digs in, it may signal they have a cost we don't see (tooling, lower volume) or that TPAC has better scale — be ready to ask why the difference exists.
Market backups listed (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify (verify capability and price before issuing RFQs) — not yet approved sources.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about the 250 mL amber PET bottle — we're paying you ₹8.49 while another supplier gives us ₹7.62 for the same item, so let's close that gap.
